transcript: Last night, I was at Atlantic Theater Company to see Buena Vista Social Club, a new musical based on the music ensemble and album of the same name. This production is described as “an homage to the artists of yesterday — the ones who survived upheaval and oppression to make the music they loved.” I had high hopes for this production when I saw it was being developed and directed by Saheem Ali of “Fat Ham” and it honestly exceeded my expectations. It’s a story of Cuban history, family, loss, but primarily it's about the vitality of music. The sparse book is in English but all the songs are kept in Spanish and the music is really the star of the show. The large ensemble of actors and musicians perform these songs with such love, urgency, and spontaneity that I was actually moved to tears despite not understanding any of the lyrics. To witness just how present and in their element everyone on stage was during this was nothing short of thrilling, and honestly it made me feel exactly how I wanna feel when I go to the theater: transported, inspired, and longing for more. With that, another playbill for my collection.
